description: A Blazor Razor Class Library that adds an AI-powered floating chat assistant to any Blazor application, built on Microsoft Agent Framework. Supports multi-level agent orchestration (tools, handoff, group chat), page navigation, UI actions, contextual memory, streaming, voice, and security — all with zero boilerplate.
releaseNotes:
1.0.0-rc.2

		Framework alignment. This release moves onto the Agent Framework 1.18.0 line and adopts two of the primitives the July 2026 guide describes. 1,423 automated tests, all green; 44 findings closed since preview.5, none open.

		=== Upgrade note - read this if you use Azure OpenAI hosted tools ==========
		- The 1.18.0 line pulls OpenAI 2.11.0, which removes a constructor that Azure.AI.OpenAI 2.9.0-beta.1 - the latest published version - still calls. The result is a MissingMethodException from AzureOpenAIClient.GetResponsesClient() at startup: the application does not fail to build and does not fail a test, it fails to boot. MentorAgent therefore holds OpenAI at 2.10.0 by pinning Microsoft.Agents.AI.Foundry to 1.17.0-preview and Microsoft.Extensions.AI.OpenAI to 10.6.0, while the framework core stays on 1.18.0. If your own project references either package directly, keep those pins or you will reintroduce the crash.

		=== NEW - skills from anywhere (MentorOptions.SkillSources) ================
		- NEW - SkillSources takes any Agent Framework AgentSkillsSource. Skills it yields reach the assistant through the same load_skill / read_skill_resource tools, the same catalogue prompt and the same gate as skills MentorAgent discovered itself - so a database, a remote catalogue, a per-tenant store or Microsoft's own AgentFileSkillsSource all work without MentorAgent knowing where they came from.
		- Composed with the framework's own decorators: AggregatingAgentSkillsSource preserves your registration order, FilteringAgentSkillsSource applies the new SkillFilter, DeduplicatingAgentSkillsSource keeps the first occurrence of a name, and CachingAgentSkillsSource is added when the new SkillsRefreshInterval is set.
		- An application skill always wins a name collision. Sources are consulted after MentorAgent's own discovery and a duplicate name is skipped with a warning naming it: a source can add a capability, never silently replace one of yours.
		- SkillFilter deliberately does not apply to your own skills. A predicate that could remove them would be a debugging trap - the skill sits in your repository and simply never appears.
		- The framework's file source did NOT replace MentorAgent's. AgentFileSkillsSource validates each SKILL.md for YAML frontmatter; MentorAgent's documented convention is a heading followed by a prose paragraph, with frontmatter before the heading ignored. Swapping the implementation would have rejected every skill file written against our own documentation. Register both and you get both dialects.
		- Requires a model. The framework's AgentSkillsSourceContext rejects a null agent and skills are discovered before the coordinator exists, so MentorAgent uses Agent when you supplied one and otherwise builds a plain agent over ChatClient. With neither, registered sources are skipped with a warning naming the fix and your own skills are unaffected.

		=== NEW - auto-approval (MentorOptions.AutoApprovalRules) ==================
		- NEW - in HitlMode.Native, AutoApprovalRules approves a tool call before any confirmation banner appears, through the framework's own ToolApprovalAgent middleware. Enabling it also enables "don't ask again": a user approval becomes a standing rule for the rest of the session.
		- NEW - MaxAutoApprovalIterations caps how many times one turn may re-run because every surfaced approval was auto-approved. Each re-run is a fresh billable model call and a per-request iteration limit restarts every time, so it cannot bound this loop.
		- SECURITY - a rule waives the prompt, never the permission. RequiredRoles is checked inside MentorAgent's own tool wrapper, which this middleware sits outside of and never sees, so a rule that approves everything still cannot let an unauthorised caller run an Admin-only action. This is a test, not a claim.
		- Opt-in. HitlMode.Native alone does not add the middleware: with no rules its only remaining effect would be "don't ask again", which silently widens what one approval covers.
		- The MCP publishing decision is unchanged and stays fail-closed. The framework's ReadOnlyToolsAutoApprovalRule turned out to be scoped to its own providers' built-in tools and cannot classify an application action, and a read-only action can still be role-restricted - so read-only never implied safe for an anonymous caller.

		=== Not adopted, and why ==================================================
		- Native memory (AgentMemory, WithMemoryIdentity, WithMemoryOwnerScoping), the harness entry points (AsHarnessAgent, HarnessAgentOptions) and EvaluatorOptions are absent from BOTH 1.6.1 and 1.18.0, the latest published release. The July 2026 guide documents APIs Microsoft has not shipped. These are a wait, not a debt, and no package bump unblocks them.
		- AIJudgeLoopEvaluator is not an evaluation-harness evaluator: it is a LoopEvaluator for LoopAgent, deciding whether an agentic loop should re-invoke the agent. It has no relationship to MentorAgent's regression harness. The roadmap row that named it has been corrected.

		=== Documentation =========================================================
		- The core README gains a worked example for every new option, plus the reference tables for the metrics snapshot and the orchestrator that rc.1 added.
